title: Sharp Causal Means under Monotone Publication Selection with Registry-Calibrated Interval Scores
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: achieved subfield below field; paper score ceiling 6.8 below 7.4; math referee pass; salvageable=false in scope.
gap_reasons: Sharpness, however, applies only when the released score cell is the entire information contract and latent score positions may vary freely within it, so the inception-cohort framing does not yet cover ordinary trial reports whose estimates, standard errors, and testing rules restrict or reconstruct the score.

The advertised computability of the mixed-law certificate is population-level: the note supplies neither an estimator nor uncertainty quantification for the signed tail functionals and potentially countable atom fibers, while its finite-sample procedure covers only the fixed coarsened identified set.

The headline censored-score refinement and endpoint-certificate theorem is compared only to broad coarsening, interval-data, and likelihood foundations; the note must identify and distinguish the closest dedicated censored-selection/rounded-score identification results before its theorem-level novelty is established.

This negative boundary result names generic rounded-score and threshold-report workflows but does not identify a specific published bibkey and claim whose refinement implication it refutes, as required for a load-bearing counterexample positioning claim.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established a sharp ordered-envelope set, endpoint certificates, a sequence-independent mixed-law refinement theorem, and conservative whole-set coverage; the D0.5 math referee passed the theorem package. The field-tier paper claim fell to subfield because the score-cell observation contract and population-level certificate do not cover ordinary trial reports or provide an operational estimator and uncertainty quantification. A field-tier continuation needs a revised score observation model with new sharpness analysis or an implemented inferential certificate, alongside the two recorded source-positioning repairs; no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: For an inception cohort of registered trials, the observable law reveals registry strata for every trial and, only for published trials, a bounded mark and the cell of a latent publication score under a fixed disjoint half-open convention.  Publication follows one common monotone exact-score rule with a maintained absolute floor but may vary arbitrarily inside each released interval.  The sharp causal-mean set is an ordered-envelope polytope.  The headline refinement theorem now characterizes, for every sequence of finite releases whose numerical mesh vanishes and without nesting, the sequence-independent split-atom limit and gives a necessary-and-sufficient two-endpoint tail-dual certificate for equality with the exact-score set.  Atomless recovery and persistent loss from a hidden tied-score atom are its two boundary corollaries.  Finite-resolution loss is controlled by selected bin mass in the one-stratum case, and simultaneous exact cell-probability envelopes provide conservative whole-set coverage while retaining empty cells.
gap: Publication probabilities can be identified from replication or meta-study variation, and registry calibration, monotone selection weights, censored \(p\)-value likelihoods, relative publication-ratio sensitivity analysis, reciprocal calibration, support-function inference, and generic coarsening inclusion are established separately. They do not determine the sharp set or the lossless-release frontier when only registry margins and an explicitly disjoint interval release of the common monotone score are available.
fill: The ordered-envelope representation supplies attainment without bin-constant weights; its tail dual supplies endpoint-specific if-and-only-if audits; the refinement results distinguish mass resolution from numerical width under a coherent cutpoint convention; and the fixed-envelope confidence procedure covers every compatible population mean, including mass in cells not observed in the sample.
